data.body: RCA and recovery evidence. Observation: HTTP receive-pack rejected valid uploads with JGit FullConnectivityChecker MissingObjectException for tree 1959f268... at 2026-09-07T21:21/21:22Z and tree 1af810df... at 2026-09-08T01:19/01:24/01:26Z; earlier log entries show the same class for aa9f407e..., fb2069..., 4fe3561..., and 1440a442.... Hypothesis A (global receive-pack outage) was falsified: scratch normal pushes from current origin/main and from the reported older base 710a606b both succeeded, creating changes 2813 and 2814, then abandoned. Hypothesis B (persistent repository corruption/missing objects) was falsified by host and in-container checks: git cat-file resolves every logged tree, refs/heads/main and refs/changes/13/2813/1, /14/2814/1, /15/2815/1 resolve as commits, and git fsck --connectivity-only --no-dangling --no-reflogs is clean. Hypothesis C (transient missing object/visibility window during rapid submit/replication under disk pressure) best fits: the failed trees correspond to recently merged/uploaded objects; the objects are now present as loose objects with mtimes matching merge/push windows, receive-pack is healthy, and no bad packs/truncated loose objects were found by fsck. Disk evidence: at investigation time root was 32%, /var/gerrit 24%, gate-scratch 29%; BuildKit cache was 5.837GB and rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high was ALARM from a prior 95% datapoint/missing-data window. Recovery: backed up /var/gerrit first with EBS snapshot snap-058fc28c74eba365e, fetched GitHub mirror main into the Gerrit repo to backfill any missing mirror-held objects, verified named trees and clean fsck, removed the temporary recovery ref, then pruned BuildKit cache to 0B (root 32% -> 25%). Verification: post-repair ordinary HEAD:refs/for/main push without --no-thin succeeded as change 2815 and was abandoned; main and refs/changes smoke refs remain readable; no Gerrit restart and no planned downtime. Prevention: feed this incident into the bounded disk-ceiling/root-disk family (scaup) and keep BuildKit/root pressure alarms meaningful rather than noisy; object-store repair should remain backup-first, fetch-from-mirror, fsck-verified, no aggressive GC until healthy.
